newsitem.title: GERMANY: German wheat prices steady on export hopes.
newsitem.headline: German wheat prices steady on export hopes.

text.p: German wheat exporters are keeping prices steady because they are hoping for new orders from eastern and southern Europe, brokers said on Wednesday.

"New trade is thin but some wheat from earlier business is still being shipped to Uzbekistan and sellers are confident there will be some follow-on deals, although North American sellers are also in the market," one said.
"We also won't reduce prices because we hope for Spanish, Portugese and perhaps Italian orders and for the EU to approve further export rebates to third countries."
The EU raised the subsidy on wheat exports to 16.59 Ecus per tonne last week from 15.97 Ecus previously.
Traders also cited as supportive a spillover effect from greater export hopes for U.S. wheat, which boosted Chicago futures prices earlier this week.
But thin turnover in Germany's internal market encouraged domestic millers to pursue just-in-time buying tactics.

Domestic feed wheat prices were shaky amid British and Danish competition and because of supply pressure in eastern Germany, which allowed raw materials buyers in the feed industry to be choosy and take their time.
Normal bread wheat (12 percent protein) was offered unchanged at 280-285 marks fob while higher quality offers remained at 285-290 and 300-302 marks, depending on protein levels.
The Hamburg grain exchange this week maintained its bread wheat price (12.5 percent, 220 hagberg) at 280 marks/tonne and its spot feed wheat price free Hamburg at 270.
Fob rye, although little traded, was steady at 250-262.50 marks because export demand held up and domestic consumer stocks were on the low side.
Fob barley prices were marked down 2.50-5.00 marks to range between 250 and 260 marks.
Brokers said Saudi Arabia was in the market and German sellers sought to compete with French and British suppliers.
Large domestic barley crops also weighed on prices, which were nearing intervention levels, the market floor.
